article_title: Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses
news_headline: Anthropic IPO raises over $81 billion in largest offering on record, topping SpaceX
post_text:
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on November 18, raising $81.3 billion, the largest public offering on record. The company debuted on Nasdaq under "ANT" at $1.5 trillion, briefly surpassing $2 trillion intraday before reversing sharply the next day, dragging the Nasdaq down 5% in what Bloomberg called a broad AI-sector "de-risking." Amazon and Google each hold stakes valued above $100 billion; a consortium including Microsoft, Nvidia, and AMD pledged a further $26 billion at the IPO price.

The frenzy around Anthropic captures something precise: capital is still willing to pay extraordinary multiples on the expectation that frontier AI becomes the defining infrastructure of the next decade. Anthropic's own run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, and the company has committed to nearly $900 billion in future compute spending, figures that make the valuation math genuinely difficult to defend on cash flows alone.

A WBR piece from earlier this year, "Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses," makes exactly this point. While markets sprint toward AI at ~30x revenue, the piece argues the real overlooked opportunity sits in unglamorous, cash-generative businesses that no one is writing IPO prospectuses about. This week gave that argument its clearest illustration yet. Full piece on the WBR website.

#WaterlooBusinessReview #AI
